Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:

Rules: year is an integer from 2007 to 2026; month is an integer from 1 to 12; c in [0, 1] is your confidence that the guess is within 6 months of the truth; 1 to 3 short cues citing the inputs.
text:
The snapshot looks like early 2010. Unemployment is 9.7%, core CPI is 1.18% and falling, and the fed funds rate is about 0.19%. Equities are up 38.6% over 12 months, which points to a window ending around Feb 2010 (the March 2009 low is about a year back).

Checking the month within that window:
- Unemployment was 9.7% in both Jan and Feb 2010, and 9.9% in Dec 2009 (the 3-month change of -0.3 implies roughly 10.0% three months earlier, which fits Oct/Nov 2009 at 10.0%/9.9%).
- Core CPI at 1.18% YoY fits Jan 2010 (1.6%?), though by Feb 2010 it was 1.3% and by Mar 2010 1.1%. The 12-month equity return of 38.6% fits Feb 2010 (S&P 500 up about 50% from Feb 2009) or Mar 2010 (up about 49%), so it is somewhat ambiguous.
- Gold rose 5.9% in the month, which fits Nov 2009 or possibly Feb 2010. The 10-year yield of 3.76% fits Feb 2010 (3.61%) or Jan 2010 (3.73%).
- Equities rose 1.5% in the month and developed ex-US fell 2.8%. This matches Feb 2010 for the S&P 500 (+3%) only loosely; it fits Jan 2010 less well, since the S&P fell 3.6% that month.
- Treasuries 20y+ rose 3.3% in the month, which suggests yields fell. Industrial production at +3.95% YoY is the first positive reading, which fits Dec 2009 (IP YoY about -1%?) or Feb 2010 (+1.5%?), so this is unclear.
- The 10-year yield rose 0.13 over 3 months. Dec 2009 had 3.84% against 3.4% in Sep, so that doesn't fit. Core CPI at 1.18% YoY with a -0.62 change over 3 months is steep, which suggests a later date, around Mar–Apr 2010.
- Unemployment at 9.7% in Apr 2010 was 9.9%, so that doesn't fit. In Aug 2010 it was 9.6%, in Jul 9.5%, and in Jun 9.4%. Core CPI at about 1.0% in Aug–Oct 2010, with equities up 38.6% over 12 months, doesn't fit.
- Equities up 38.6% over 12 months fits Feb 2010 or Mar 2010. March 2010 had an S&P gain of +6%, so Feb 2010 fits better. A 3-month equity return of 11.1% is also consistent with Feb 2010.

I'll go with Feb 2010.
